source.scope: Seven fixtures in test/core.test.mjs and test/codex-provider.test.mjs

reasons.Q1: All original assertions, expected data, names and provider calls are preserved. Only the two scoped test files change. Explicit try/finally wraps the seven fixtures and T1 writer setup. XDG restoration remains before owned-directory removal. Both complete files execute 162 tests with no skips or failures.
reasons.Q2: Fourteen normal probes cover every scoped fixture twice. Each raw record shows exactly one target directory created and successfully removed by an exact owned rmSync call; all sentinels remain unchanged. Both T1 passes record writer close before removal.
reasons.Q3: All seven assertion-failure probes plus the second runtime probe with XDG absent execute one failing test with the expected sentinel. All owned directories are removed. In-process initial/final XDG records match, including the absent-value case.
reasons.Q4: The T1 writer-setup probe records injection at sequence 3, successful closure of writer-1 at sequence 4 and exact owned removal at sequence 5. The T2 writeFileSync setup failure preserves its sentinel and removes the exact fixture. Both run as single expected failures.

reasons: Both configured MCP arms made zero formal MCP calls despite passing real query readiness.
CodeFacts experienced two confirmed command-launch policy rejections; patch acceptance cannot remove this execution interference.
One natural-choice task and one attempt per arm do not establish a general causal efficiency effect.

accounting.engineeringTokensNote: Controller, reviewer, setup and evaluator engineering usage was not aggregated at this cutoff; recorded agent tokens are not total project cost.
accounting.elapsedMeasurement: Formal process launch to exit, including tool startup and all within-attempt recovery.
accounting.outputMeasurement: Logged shell output bytes may precede model-visible truncation; not tokens or exact context size.

review.executionAuditNote: Ordinary and CodeGraph warnings were manually cleared; CodeFacts policy rejections remain substantive. The exact rejecting policy clause is not present in the logs.

delivery.selectionReason: A and C are byte-identical. Their early test teardown registration covers setup and assertion failures with smaller changes and less reindentation, while retaining the focused inner writer finally. B is also correct and acceptable; its broader try/finally reindentation adds review churn without a demonstrated correctness gain for this frozen task.

decision.basis: A real maintenance repair was delivered. This task supplies a natural non-use observation and no queried retrieval defect; no tool-efficiency win was established.
decision.nextTrigger: New independently sourced consumer work with an explicit decision, or a reproducible present-source correctness/retrieval/install failure.
